solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: We must admit trade is mismanaged in bank? (9)

indicatorNotes.must admit: to admit is to let in, so WE takes the rest inside
indicatorNotes.mismanaged: handled badly, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as printed; it wraps the rest
TRADE IS rearranged

annotation.surface: A complaint that the trading at a bank has been badly run.
annotation.walkthrough: The bank in the surface is a financial one; the answer is a riverbank, which is why the question mark is there.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a riverbank is one kind of waterside, and the question mark admits the narrowing.

entries.clue: One desiring less herb to begin with and more sage (5)

indicatorNotes.less: minus, so a letter is taken away
indicatorNotes.to begin with: what comes first in herb is its opening letter

blocks.note: one who wishes
first letter of herb, removed from WISHER

annotation.surface: A cook wanting less of one herb and more of the herb sage.
annotation.walkthrough: Herb and sage sit together to suggest the kitchen, but sage here is the adjective, not the plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sage as an adjective means wise, and the comparative matches the -ER ending.

entries.clue: Path to secure a victory for Labour (7)

indicatorNotes.to secure: the path holds the other letters fast inside it

blocks.note: a trail is a path
A plus V for victory, placed inside TRAIL

annotation.surface: A political strategy for winning an election for the Labour Party.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Labour look like the British political party; it is plain hard work.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: travail is painful toil, and labour carries the same sense of hard effort.

entries.clue: Rock embracing European form for example (4,5)

indicatorNotes.embracing: hugging, so ROLL goes around the rest

blocks.note: to rock is to roll, as a ship does
standard abbreviation
a mode is a form or manner

annotation.surface: A geology note about rock enclosing a European formation.
annotation.walkthrough: Rock and form suggest geology; rock is really the verb, the side-to-side motion of a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense 'someone to follow': setting an example is what a role model does.

entries.clue: Unbeatable chorizo served up by Puck? (11)

indicatorNotes.served up: in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: Puck is the mischievous sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream
a Spanish sausage, jokingly 'el banger'; a banger is a sausage

annotation.surface: A menu boast about chorizo served by someone named Puck.
annotation.walkthrough: Chorizo is Spanish, so the setter dresses 'banger' (British slang for a sausage) with the Spanish article EL. The question mark flags both that joke and Puck as a sample imp.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something impregnable cannot be taken or overcome, so it cannot be beaten.

entries.clue: Decline leads to everyone being broke (3)

indicatorNotes.leads to: the leading letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of Everyone Being Broke

annotation.surface: Economic decline leaves everyone short of money.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as cause and effect in an economy; the clue is only initials after the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym taken from the tide: the ebb is the tide going out, so it stands for any falling away.

entries.clue: End of Siegfried in Ring Cycle (5)

indicatorNotes.End of: take the last letter of Siegfried
indicatorNotes.in: that letter goes inside the ring

blocks.note: a ring of bells is a peal
last letter of Siegfried, set inside PEAL

annotation.surface: The final part of Wagner's opera Siegfried within his Ring Cycle.
annotation.walkthrough: Siegfried is the third opera of Wagner's Ring Cycle, so 'Ring Cycle' reads as one title; it splits into wordplay and definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Cycle is a verb here, riding a bicycle, and that is done by working the pedals.

entries.clue: Greek troops not willing to participate (5)

indicatorNotes.not: without, so those letters come away

blocks.note: a platoon is a unit of soldiers
if you're on, you're up for it; removed from PLATOON

annotation.surface: Greek soldiers refusing to join in a campaign.
annotation.walkthrough: Greek is the definition on its own: a famous Greek. 'Willing to participate' is ON, as in 'Are you on for tonight?'
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the philosopher is one particular Greek, the nationality standing for the man.

entries.clue: Reversing identity, man’s female (7)

indicatorNotes.Reversing: turn the letters for identity back to front

blocks.note: ID is short for identity
to man a desk is to staff it

annotation.surface: A gender swap: a man's identity turned round becomes a woman's.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests gender reversal, but man is the verb to staff and the 's is just 'is' joining the parts to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the distaff side of a family is the female line, from the spinning staff women used.

entries.clue: Deposit from freemasons close to Craft? (9)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close, or end, of Craft is its last letter

blocks.note: freemasons meet in lodges, so they are lodge men
last letter of Craft

annotation.surface: Money handed over by freemasons, near to the Craft, as they call freemasonry.
annotation.walkthrough: Freemasons call their movement the Craft, which is why the surface hangs together and why the question mark is there.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from banking: you lodge money with a bank, so the act or sum lodged is a deposit.

entries.clue: Leaving a duck, everyone tucks into exclusive seafood (7)

indicatorNotes.Leaving: going without, so one O is dropped
indicatorNotes.tucks into: slips inside, so ALL goes inside SCOOP

blocks.note: a scoop is an exclusive news story
put inside SCOOP to make SCALLOOP
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O; one O is removed

annotation.surface: A diner skips the duck and everyone digs into a special seafood dish.
annotation.walkthrough: Duck and tucks into keep us at the dinner table; duck is zero, the cricket score, and exclusive is a journalist's scoop.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the scallop is one shellfish among the many that count as seafood.

entries.clue: Slowly stewed beef initially increased in intensity (7)

indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so the first letter of beef

blocks.note: first letter of beef
raised = turned up

annotation.surface: A recipe: beef slowly stewed, with the heat turned up at first.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a cooking instruction, so the definition hides at the front in plain view.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from cooking: braising is slow cooking in a little liquid in a closed pot, close kin to stewing.

entries.clue: Field Bernabéu team, missing second half (5)

indicatorNotes.missing second half: drop the back half of the name

blocks.note: the Bernabéu is Real Madrid's stadium; its second half ADRID goes

annotation.surface: Real Madrid putting out a side without its second-half players.
annotation.walkthrough: Field reads as the football verb, to put out a team; it is the noun, a sphere of activity.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of a domain of knowledge: someone's field is their realm.

entries.clue: Psychic powers in later years keeping old in secret work (9)

indicatorNotes.keeping: holding, so IN AGE keeps O inside it

blocks.note: extrasensory perception
in age, i.e. when older
standard abbreviation, placed inside INAGE after the I

annotation.surface: Someone who in old age uses their psychic gifts for covert work.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a spy with second sight. The O slips in between the I and the N of IN AGE.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: spying is work done in secret, so the phrase paraphrases the trade.

entries.clue: Animal long dead at Clyde port reanimated (11)

indicatorNotes.reanimated: brought back to life in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: A long-dead creature brought back to life at a Scottish harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: The Clyde is the river of Glasgow. 'Reanimated' neatly suits a creature long dead, which is what makes the surface work.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the pterodactyl is a flying reptile extinct for millions of years.

entries.clue: Creature hunting near ground, moving left to right (3)

indicatorNotes.moving left to right: L (left) moves from the front to the right-hand end

blocks.note: low = close to the ground; its L goes to the end

annotation.surface: An animal hunting close to the ground, moving across from left to right.
annotation.walkthrough: Left is L, the usual abbreviation, and right means the end of the word. Barn owls hunt by flying low over fields.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the owl is a bird of prey, a creature that hunts.

entries.clue: Powerful group of 50 swelling fantastic gay choir (9)

indicatorNotes.swelling: L makes the other letters swell by sitting inside them
indicatorNotes.fantastic: wild, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: GAY CHOIR rearranged
Roman numeral fifty, set inside after the O

annotation.surface: Fifty voices joining a fabulous gay choir makes it a powerful group.
annotation.walkthrough: Of links the definition to the wordplay; 50 is the Roman L, which swells the anagram by one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: an oligarchy is rule by a few, a small group holding power.

entries.clue: Writer of Aeneid led astray (6,5)

indicatorNotes.astray: gone off course, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: The author of Virgil's Aeneid having been misled.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks for Virgil, the Aeneid's poet; the 'of' is part of the fodder, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Defoe, author of Robinson Crusoe, is one writer.

entries.clue: Single-minded inspector with Jaguar perhaps in Endeavour (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the inspector and the cat go inside the endeavour

blocks.note: a deed is an undertaking or effort
Detective Inspector
a jaguar is a big cat, placed after DI inside DEED

annotation.surface: Inspector Morse, first name Endeavour, famous for driving a Jaguar, is single-minded.
annotation.walkthrough: Endeavour is Inspector Morse's first name and the title of the prequel series, and Morse drove a Jaguar; here it is just an effort.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone dedicated to a cause is wholly committed, pursuing one aim.

entries.clue: True crime work incorporated elderly relatives (2,4,5)

blocks.note: Inc. is the abbreviation for incorporated
old = elderly
your blood is your family, as in 'blood is thicker than water'

annotation.surface: A criminal case involving old family members, taken into a book.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a book title: the answer is the book that founded the true-crime genre.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Truman Capote's 1966 account of a Kansas murder is the classic true-crime book.

entries.clue: Willing rider Richard endlessly breaking wind (7)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: without its end, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.breaking: bursting into, so DIC goes inside COIL

blocks.note: to wind is to coil
Dick, short for Richard, loses its K and goes inside COIL

annotation.surface: A horse-rider called Richard who keeps passing wind.
annotation.walkthrough: Willing rider reads as an eager horseman; wind is the verb, rhyming with find.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a rider is a clause added to a document, and willing means relating to a will, so a rider to a will.

entries.clue: Copper beginning to tire in nick (3)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so tire gives up only its T

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
first letter of tire

annotation.surface: A police officer beginning to flag in the police station.
annotation.walkthrough: Copper and nick are both British slang from policing (a policeman, a police station), but copper is the metal and nick is a small wound.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to nick your finger is to cut it slightly, and the noun works the same way.

entries.clue: Comfort maiden Zeus seduced for so long (7)

blocks.note: to cheer is to comfort
Io was a mortal woman loved by Zeus in Greek myth

annotation.surface: A young woman consoled after Zeus seduced her for a long time.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface dwells on Zeus's affair and makes 'so long' a length of time, but it is a farewell.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: cheerio is a casual British goodbye, just as so long is an informal parting.

entries.clue: Constellation also wandered: Alpha moved to the east (9)

indicatorNotes.moved to the east: east is the right-hand side of a map, so the A goes to the end

blocks.note: and = also
ROAMED with its A (alpha) sent to the end

annotation.surface: A star map note: a constellation drifting, with its brightest star moved eastward.
annotation.walkthrough: Alpha is the NATO word for A, and in an across clue east means to the right, so the A of ROAMED shifts to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Andromeda is one constellation, named after the chained princess of Greek myth.

entries.clue: Board somehow communicating green light from Macron, then Merz (5)

blocks.note: French for yes; Macron is the French president
German for yes; Merz is the German chancellor

annotation.surface: A board gives approval passed from Macron to Merz.
annotation.walkthrough: The board's name is French and German yes run together; the definition's second half hints at messages from the dead.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a Ouija board is used at séances, supposedly passing messages from spirits.

entries.clue: Best study hard to get grip on English (5)

indicatorNotes.to get grip on: to grip is to hold, so CRAM holds E

blocks.note: to cram is to study intensively
standard abbreviation, held inside CRAM

annotation.surface: Advice that the best pupils study hard to master English.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exam advice; the definition is the noun, the pick of the bunch.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: cream rises to the top of milk, so the cream of any group is its finest part.

entries.clue: Density in low cloud that’s thick (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in means within, so D is placed inside the word for low cloud

blocks.note: mist is cloud at ground level
d is the symbol for density in physics, placed inside MIST

annotation.surface: Thick, dense low cloud.
annotation.walkthrough: Thick suggests dense fog; it is the noun, as in 'in the thick of things'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be in the thick of the action is to be in its midst, its busiest part.

entries.clue: Drug lord who ran to restrain murderer (7)

indicatorNotes.to restrain: hold in, so COE holds CAIN

blocks.note: Lord (Sebastian) Coe, Olympic middle-distance runner
Cain killed Abel in Genesis; placed inside COE

annotation.surface: A drug baron trying to hold back a killer.
annotation.walkthrough: Drug lord is a set phrase, but it splits: drug is the definition and lord who ran is Seb Coe, the British runner turned peer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: cocaine, the stimulant from coca leaves, is one drug.

entries.clue: Line this writer grasps when climbing tree (3)

indicatorNotes.grasps: to grasp is to hold in the hand, so the writer's ME closes around L
indicatorNotes.when climbing: in a down clue, climbing reads the letters upwards

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself
standard abbreviation, held inside ME

annotation.surface: The writer grabs a rope while climbing a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: This writer is the setter, so ME; the tree is both where the climbing happens and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the elm is one broadleaf tree, once common in English hedgerows.

entries.clue: Did coach express disapproval? Nothing revolutionary (7)

blocks.note: tut is the click of the tongue for disapproval
zero
a red is a communist revolutionary

annotation.surface: A question whether the coach tutted, answered with nothing revolutionary.
annotation.walkthrough: Did coach looks like the start of a question; it is the past tense that TUTORED matches.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a coach gives private teaching, which is what a tutor does, and 'did' supplies the past tense.

entries.clue: Agent on vacation was resting around Black Sea resort (5)

indicatorNotes.on vacation: vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters
indicatorNotes.around: turned round, so the combined letters run backwards

blocks.note: outer letters of AgenT
past tense of lie; AT + LAY then reversed

annotation.surface: A spy on holiday lounging around a Black Sea resort.
annotation.walkthrough: On vacation reads as holiday, fitting the resort; it is an instruction to empty the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Crimean town, famous for the 1945 Allied conference, is one Black Sea resort.

entries.clue: Tactless whisky promotion French king stops (9)

indicatorNotes.stops: plugs, so AD ROI fills the middle of MALT

blocks.note: a malt is a malt whisky
an advertisement promotes
French for king; AD ROI goes inside MALT

annotation.surface: A crass whisky advert that a French king puts a stop to.
annotation.walkthrough: Stops reads as the king banning the advert; it works like a cork stopping a bottle, plugging the gap.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: maladroit means clumsy, and in social dealings clumsiness is tactlessness.
